Great question! There are actually two different stories about who started the very first Olympic Games.

One story says **King Pelops** started them. He was a prince who won a chariot race to marry a beautiful princess named Hippodamia.

Another story says **Heracles** started them. He organized the games to honor his dad after he finished all his 12 labors.

Nobody knows for sure which story is true! But we do know the very first Olympic Games happened way back in 776 BCE in Greece, and they were held to honor Zeus, who was the king of all the gods.

story_name: Who decides what robots look like?
story_description: Who decides what robots look like? How do robots work and move? How are they controlled? And are robots alive? We tackle all your robot questions in this episode, and we’re taking a field trip to a local factory that uses hundreds of robots to help humans do their jobs. GlobalFoundries, in Essex Junction, Vermont makes microchips that go in all kinds of electronics. In fact, if your adults have a smartphone, more than likely it has a chip made at this very facility. Engineers Adrien Plouffe and Lucy White work with the robots at GlobalFoundries and answer your questions about robots, including: Why are robots made of metal? Why do people like robots? Do robots cry?
